headline: Alphabet's earnings disappoint and drag tech lower last night, while oil spikes on Middle East tensions and the ASX holds firm today.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS fell another 4% today to $2.64, continuing its brutal slide — down over 60% from your entry. Lithium prices remain depressed globally and there's no near-term catalyst to change that. The long-term EV story is still intact but the market is in no rush to re-rate lithium miners right now.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI dropped 2.79% today, dragged down by weakness in Alphabet (Google) after its earnings disappointed last night. The ETF holds a basket of AI-exposed stocks, so when big names like GOOG sell off, GXAI follows. The broader AI sector remains the long-term bet here.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft actually beat earnings expectations last night on both revenue and profit, driven by AI growth. But the stock still fell 1.9% — likely caught in the broader tech sell-off triggered by Google's weak results. Analysts noted investors are viewing Microsoft's AI spending more favourably than Alphabet's, so the relative damage was limited.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE dipped 1.16% today. Emerging market ETFs tend to slide when global risk appetite weakens — and with the NASDAQ down sharply last night and oil spiking on Middle East tensions, investors pulled back from riskier assets like emerging markets.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google fell 1.27% last night following earnings that disappointed the market — reports citing a $9 billion cash burn and weaker-than-expected results. Bloomberg noted it wasn't a crisis, but the market punished the stock hard. This dragged the whole tech sector lower.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS edged down 0.69% today, reflecting last night's sharp NASDAQ sell-off (down 2.67%). As a US total market ETF, VTS tracks US equities broadly, so a rough night on Wall Street flows straight through to today's ASX price.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG dipped a modest 0.25% today. As a diversified fund holding global and Australian shares, bonds, and property, it cushions the blow when individual markets wobble — exactly what it's designed to do.

movers.name: DHHF
movers.note: DHHF slipped just 0.22% today — essentially flat. As a broad, all-in-one diversified ETF, it's well-insulated from single-stock or single-sector moves. Nothing to worry about here.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two dipped a quiet 0.59% last night with no major news driving the move. GTA 6 hype continues — reports suggest the game's map will be nearly as large as GTA 4, GTA 5, and Red Dead Redemption 2 combined. A viral 'watermark leak' was debunked by insiders. The long-term GTA 6 launch catalyst remains intact.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Pilbara Minerals holding at painful lows
watch_today.detail: PLS closed at $2.64 today, down 4% in a session. You're down 60%+ on this position. Lithium prices remain weak globally and there's no imminent recovery catalyst. But the long-term electrification and battery storage thesis hasn't gone away — this is a cyclical downturn, not a structural collapse of the industry. Sit tight if you believe in the multi-year story, but be honest with yourself about your conviction.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — AI ETF hit by Google earnings weakness
watch_today.detail: GXAI dropped 2.79% today largely because Alphabet's disappointing earnings last night rattled the broader AI sector. You're down 15% overall on this position. The AI theme is still very much in play — Google just launched Gemini 4 Carbon which is topping benchmarks — but short-term volatility will follow big earnings swings. Long-term hold.

watch_today.title: GOOG — Alphabet earnings disappoint but not a crisis
watch_today.detail: GOOG fell 1.27% last night after earnings flagged a $9 billion cash burn and came in below expectations. Bloomberg's take was 'wobbly quarter, not a crisis.' Meanwhile Google released Gemini 4 Carbon, which is beating GPT-6 and Claude on most benchmarks. The long-term ad and AI business is still strong. A small position and the thesis is intact — hold.

watch_today.title: MSFT — Beat earnings but still sold off
watch_today.detail: Microsoft beat Q1 estimates on both revenue and profit, driven by AI cloud growth, but fell 1.9% caught in the tech sector sell-off. Investors are viewing Microsoft's AI spending more favourably than Alphabet's. You're up 17% overall on this position. Nothing has changed with the long-term case — this is noise.

watch_today.title: Oil spike — watch for flow-on effects
watch_today.detail: Crude oil jumped 2.4% last night to US$104.45 a barrel as tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz amid the ongoing Iran conflict. If this escalates, expect energy costs to rise and inflation to stay stickier — which means the RBA could keep rates higher for longer. Worth watching through the week.

watch_today.title: RBA rate hike expected on Melbourne Cup Day (Tuesday)
watch_today.detail: Markets are pricing in a fifth RBA interest rate hike on Tuesday — Melbourne Cup Day. A sixth hike is now a 50/50 bet according to Market Index. A major bank has said an Australian recession is now 'a coin toss.' Higher rates mean continued pressure on household budgets and could weigh on growth stocks in your portfolio. Key event to watch Tuesday.

world.summary: A deadly train crash in Spain, oil spiking on Iran-related Strait of Hormuz incidents, Trump's escalating legal battles over US elections, and China's clean tech exports are the big global stories today.

stories.title: At least 68 dead in Spain's second major train crash this year
stories.why_it_matters: Spain has suffered its second major train disaster of 2026, with at least 68 people confirmed dead. The crash adds to growing public pressure on Spain's rail network and government over infrastructure safety. This follows an earlier fatal incident earlier this year, making it one of Europe's deadliest years for rail travel in recent memory.

stories.title: Tankers strike mines in Strait of Hormuz as Iran conflict escalates
stories.why_it_matters: Tankers have struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz — the narrow waterway through which about 20% of the world's oil supply passes — as the Iran conflict continues. This sent crude oil prices up 2.4% last night to over US$104 a barrel. BP also reported an 18-year profit high thanks to higher oil refining margins driven by the Iran war. If the Strait gets blockaded or further disrupted, petrol prices globally — including in Australia — would spike sharply.

stories.title: Trump administration opens criminal investigation over alleged noncitizen voting in California
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration has launched a criminal investigation into alleged non-citizen voting in California, escalating its legal battles against states ahead of the 2026 US midterm elections. A federal judge has also ordered Trump officials to outline election-related demands sent to states. With US midterms approaching, these moves signal a highly charged and contested political environment — the outcome could shift the balance of power in Congress and affect US economic and foreign policy direction.

stories.title: China's record clean tech exports making a big dent in global emissions
stories.why_it_matters: A new report says China's record-breaking exports of solar panels, electric vehicles, and batteries are having a measurable impact on global carbon emissions. China is now the world's largest exporter of clean energy technology, which is both a climate win and a geopolitical flashpoint — particularly as Western nations impose tariffs to protect domestic manufacturers. For Australian investors, this is relevant to the lithium and minerals sector, as China's clean tech dominance shapes global demand for battery materials.

stories.title: Crypto worth billions frozen after suspected Binance hack
stories.why_it_matters: Billions of dollars worth of cryptocurrency has been frozen following a suspected hack of Binance, one of the world's largest crypto exchanges. Authorities are investigating. This is a reminder of the ongoing security vulnerabilities in crypto markets — if you hold any crypto assets, it's worth checking your exchange's security status and considering whether assets held on exchanges are safe.

markets.summary: The ASX held up well today, gaining 0.18% to close at 8,908 — a quiet Friday finish. Last night on Wall Street was ugly though, with the NASDAQ down 2.67% and the S&P 500 off 1.58%, mostly driven by Alphabet's earnings disappointment. Oil jumped 2.4% on Middle East tensions, while gold fell 2.9% — a big drop for a safe haven. The Aussie dollar slipped slightly to US70.19 cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Held firm today, relatively insulated from last night's US tech sell-off.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session — fell sharply on Alphabet's earnings disappointment.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Last night's session — tech-heavy index took the brunt of Google's sell-off.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Spiked last night as tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Unusual drop for a safe-haven asset — possibly profit-taking or repositioning around oil and rates.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar slipped slightly — a weaker AUD makes your US holdings worth a bit more in AUD terms.

politics.summary: Big domestic stories today: a major bank says an Australian recession is now a coin toss, the RBA is expected to hike rates again on Melbourne Cup Day Tuesday, Labor wants to ban AI data centres from suburban areas, and PM Albanese is defending a $10 billion EU trade deal.

stories.title: Australian recession now 'a coin toss', says major bank
stories.why_it_matters: A major Australian bank has warned that the chance of a domestic recession is now roughly 50/50. The combination of rising interest rates, cost of living pressures, and weak consumer spending is squeezing the economy. If we do tip into recession, expect higher unemployment, falling property prices, and weaker returns from growth assets like shares.

stories.title: RBA set to hike rates again on Melbourne Cup Day — and a sixth rise is a 50/50 bet
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank of Australia is widely expected to deliver its fifth interest rate hike at Tuesday's Melbourne Cup Day board meeting. Markets are also pricing a 50% chance of a sixth hike to follow. Each rise increases the cost of variable-rate mortgages — someone with a $600,000 loan is now paying hundreds more per month than two years ago. Higher rates also tend to weigh on share prices, particularly growth stocks.

stories.title: Labor to ban AI data centres from suburban Australia
stories.why_it_matters: The Labor government is moving to ban AI data centres from being built in suburban residential areas. As the AI industry booms globally, data centres are springing up everywhere — but they're power-hungry, noisy, and generate significant heat. The ban would push them to industrial or regional zones. This affects the rollout of AI infrastructure in Australia and could influence costs for tech companies operating here.

stories.title: PM Albanese defends $10 billion EU trade deal amid Coalition criticism
stories.why_it_matters: Prime Minister Albanese is defending a $10 billion free trade deal with the European Union, which the Coalition is criticising over farm market access and climate-linked trade clauses. The deal could open up significant export opportunities for Australian goods in Europe, but farmers are concerned about whether they'll genuinely get better access to EU markets, and some businesses are wary of the climate conditions attached.

ai.summary: Google dropped its most powerful AI model yet — Gemini 4 Carbon — which is beating both GPT-6 and Claude on most benchmarks, though it's not publicly available yet. Meanwhile Microsoft is quietly winning the AI spending confidence game, and AI regulation is heating up in Japan and Switzerland.

stories.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon — beats GPT-6 and Claude on most benchmarks
stories.why_it_matters: Google has launched Gemini 4 Carbon, its most advanced AI model yet, and early benchmark results show it outperforming OpenAI's GPT-6 and Anthropic's Claude on most tests. One specific focus is cybersecurity — the model is designed to find and fix software security flaws automatically. The catch: it's not publicly available yet. CEO Sundar Pichai's launch comments reportedly put pressure on two rival AI companies. This matters for your GOOG and GXAI holdings — Google is still very much in the AI race.

stories.title: Why Microsoft's AI spending is seen more favourably than Google's by investors
stories.why_it_matters: Both Microsoft and Alphabet reported earnings last night, and both are spending heavily on AI infrastructure. But investors reacted very differently — Microsoft's stock fell only modestly while Google tanked. The reason: Microsoft's Azure cloud AI revenues are growing strongly and the market trusts its spending roadmap, while Google's AI investment is seen as burning cash without the same clear return yet. Microsoft is trimming its AI capex outlook to $170 billion, which reassured investors.

stories.title: TBC launches 'Mischief' — a new AI video model built on Wan 2.2
stories.why_it_matters: A new AI video generation model called 'Mischief' has launched, built on the Wan 2.2 architecture — which is derived from studying neuron activity patterns. In plain English, it can generate realistic video from text prompts or images, with reportedly better motion and physics than earlier models. AI video generation is becoming a genuine creative tool, with implications for advertising, film, and content creation industries.

stories.title: Japan's cyberattack surge fuels debate over AI regulation and data security
stories.why_it_matters: Japan is seeing a surge in AI-assisted cyberattacks, and it's prompting a national debate about whether to tighten AI regulation and data security laws. As AI tools become more accessible, they're also being used by hackers to automate and scale attacks. This is a global issue — Australia has faced its own high-profile data breaches — and may accelerate regulatory action in the Asia-Pacific region.

sport.summary: It's Rugby League World Cup season — England are in deep trouble after a shock loss to Papua New Guinea, while the AFL's 2027 fixture has just dropped with Sydney the big winner. The NRL Grand Final between the Roosters and Knights ended in a thriller — Roosters won 19-18.

stories.title: England stunned by Papua New Guinea Kumuls — needs miracle to reach RLWC semis
stories.why_it_matters: England have been knocked over by the Papua New Guinea Kumuls in a major Rugby League World Cup upset, and Fox Sports reports they're now saying 'we're going home' — needing a miracle result to reach the semi-finals. PNG's gritty win is one of the tournament's biggest shocks and a massive moment for Pacific island rugby league.

stories.title: NRL Grand Final: Roosters defeat Knights 19-18 in thriller
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters have claimed the 2026 NRL premiership, defeating the Newcastle Knights 19-18 in a nail-biting Grand Final at Accor Stadium. One point the difference — it doesn't get much closer than that. A heartbreaking loss for the Knights who came within a point of claiming their first title since 2001.

stories.title: AFL 2027 fixture drops — Sydney big winner, St Kilda snubbed
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL's 2027 season fixture has been released with Sydney the biggest winner in terms of primetime scheduling. St Kilda has been described as 'completely snubbed' in the prime broadcast slots. Primetime games mean more exposure, more revenue, and larger crowds — so fixture allocation is a genuine competitive advantage for clubs.

stories.title: Casualty ward: Kalyn Ponga still a chance for Knights; Katoa cleared
stories.why_it_matters: Kalyn Ponga (Knights) is still listed as a chance to play despite injury concerns, while Tesi Katoa has been given the all-clear. Injury news in the lead-up to finals footy can flip results — Ponga's fitness is always a major talking point given he's one of the NRL's most damaging players.

stories.title: GWS land major retention coup as star shuts down AFL interest
stories.why_it_matters: GWS Giants have pulled off a significant retention win, locking in a star player who had attracted interest from rival AFL clubs. The player has reportedly shut down any talk of a move and recommitted to the Giants. In a competition where list management is everything, keeping your best players is as important as drafting new ones.
